title: The execution continuum as widening visibility
caption: Every optimization has a visibility prerequisite. Eager reveals one operation, so fusion and memory planning are impossible by construction. Graph capture reveals a region and enables fusion inside it. AOT export reveals the whole program, enabling arena allocation and full scheduling. A vendor engine adds fixed shapes and one target, unlocking hand-tuned kernels. Moving right buys optimization and pays in flexibility - and each position maps to a framework idiom: Python loops, torch.compile/jax.jit, SavedModel/ONNX export, TensorRT/TFLM.

title: The decode step the host can't feed
caption: One batch-one GPT-2 XL decode step in three clockings: the device can read the 3 GB of FP16 weights in ~0.9 ms, driver launches alone take ~2.9 ms (576 kernels x ~5 us), and full eager issue with Python dispatch takes ~8.6 ms. The accelerator spends ~90% of the step waiting for instructions. The gap between the first bar and the last is the framework's latency contribution.

title: The tape builds the peak, backward unwinds it
caption: Forward execution records ops and retains the tensors each backward rule will need, so the saved-activation stack grows one tower per layer and peaks exactly where forward ends. Backward consumes the towers in reverse order, freeing each as it passes. Checkpointing chooses to re-record a segment during backward rather than hold it - the compute-for-memory trade at the heart of training memory.
